nodes.question: Are both the mug and the headphones visible enough to compare their positions?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the mug and headphones are identifiable and their relative positions can be judged; fail if the image clearly shows either is absent or the comparison is impossible; unknown if visibility or identification is inconclusive.
nodes.binding: Use only the image to identify the mug and headphones and assess whether their relative placement is observable. This establishes evidence availability, not fulfillment.

nodes.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. For R1, complete if this check passes; absent if it fails and no requested change has progressed; partial if the mug has moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right; unknown if required evidence remains unresolved. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what evidence shows whether the original blue mug has moved toward or to the right of the headphones, rather than remaining at its source location while another mug appears on the right?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the original blue mug is identifiable in the edited image and is visibly to the right of the headphones. Fail if clear visual evidence shows the original blue mug remains at or near its source location and a distinct mug is on the right. Unknown if the original mug's identity or location cannot be determined. Report any visible displacement toward the right even if it does not reach the target; do not infer movement from the presence of a right-side mug alone.
nodes.binding: Compare source and edited images. Use the source blue mug's distinctive appearance and original position left of the headphones as anchors. Inspect the edited image for that mug's location and any distinct additional mug. Distinguish observed displacement from uncertain identity; do not treat ambiguity as evidence of no progress.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Compose with s1, s2, and s3. Complete if s2 establishes the requested right-side relation; do not require proof of source-object continuity for that final-state requirement. Partial if the requested relation is not established but s3 provides evidence that the original mug moved toward the right, or s2 shows a right-side mug while s3 establishes it is an addition and the original mug remains elsewhere. Absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress. Unknown when necessary evidence is unresolved and neither completion nor progress/absence is established. Unrelated edits do not count.
nodes.binding: Target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.. Reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
